channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: INSEAD launches Thrive Lab with $3 million from Google.org and DeepMind — to study how people flourish alongside AI
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: INSEAD announced on October 30, 2026 that Google.org and Google DeepMind will fund its new Thrive Lab with US$3 million, to research how people and organisations can flourish — in learning, work, and relationships — as AI reshapes daily life.

item.title: Envision’s Tianji tops ECMWF’s AI Weather Quest: a physics-AI model aimed at the 19–25 day window
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Envision announced on October 30, 2026 that its Tianji weather foundation model ranked first overall in ECMWF’s AI Weather Quest, beating nearly 20 teams across every assessed metric for days 19–25 — the subseasonal window where forecasts get hardest, and where wind and solar planning lives.

item.title: Reddit says Google's AI Mode sends it no traffic — and will test locking casual browsing behind a login
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Reddit's search referrals fell by more than a million a week in October, its US audience shrank for the first time since its IPO, and its answer is to test a mostly logged-in site — trading reach for control over the community archive that AI companies want to scrape.

item.title: Lightpanda hands-on: the headless browser built for AI agents, from first fetch to a replayable scrape
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Lightpanda is a headless browser written from scratch in Zig for agents and automation — no Chromium, a fraction of the memory. This guide installs the nightly binary, fetches JavaScript-rendered pages to Markdown, extracts structured data, and turns a REPL session into a replayable script you can run without any model at all.

item.title: Point your coding agent at your repo and get a threat model you can actually check: hands-on with Grim Prompter
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Grim Prompter (jmanico/grim-prompter, MIT, 212 GitHub stars) turns Claude Code, Codex or any coding agent into a threat-model reviewer: 36 architecture workflows and 29 method prompts, installed by linking one skill, run with a single slash command, and checked against your code with file-and-line citations. This guide installs it, runs a quick API model, challenges the findings, and keeps the model current as the code changes.

item.title: Cognizant commits more than 25,000 professionals to OpenAI delivery with a new Frontier Capability Group
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Cognizant announced on October 30, 2026 that it has formed an OpenAI Frontier Capability Group of more than 25,000 professionals to deliver Codex and ChatGPT into enterprise software, modernization, and customer operations — starting with methods it tested inside its own sales teams.

item.title: A six-year-old designed a unicorn game and Claude Sonnet built it in under a month — Reddit's verdict on the father-daughter build
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: A father and his six-year-old daughter designed a pixel-art unicorn sandbox together, with Claude Sonnet 5.5 writing the code — and a 2:33 gameplay clip has r/ClaudeAI debating what, exactly, deserves the amazement.

item.title: Your laptop is the API: run a local LLM server with llama-cpp-python and a 398 MB GGUF model
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: llama-cpp-python turns a 398 MB GGUF model into a local OpenAI-compatible API: this guide loads Qwen2.5-0.5B on CPU, streams tokens, forces JSON-schema output, and serves it on localhost — with every command verified and one honest model failure included.

item.title: Waymo’s next robotaxi is a Toyota: factory-built bZ4X fleet to test in Japan in 2027, UK to follow
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Toyota and Waymo will begin testing a fleet of autonomous Toyota bZ4X SUVs in Japan in 2027, built and fitted with Waymo’s driving hardware at Toyota’s Takaoka plant, with deployment in the UK and other Waymo markets planned for later years.

item.title: OpenAI rewrites its Model Spec around five values — and admits its models do not follow it yet
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: OpenAI has rewritten the public rulebook for how its models should behave, organizing it around five values headed by faithfulness to human intent. The document now also spells out hard limits on autonomous agents — and, in the same breath, concedes that today’s models do not live up to it yet.

item.title: Blind the agent reading your code: hands-on with BLA, the open-source shield against AI reverse-engineering
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: BLA, a five-day-old MIT-licensed shield created on October 25, 2026, hardens your shipped JavaScript against AI reverse-engineering agents: one audit, one protect command, and the demo file's exposure score fell from 81 to 2 while its output stayed identical. This guide runs every command and shows the real numbers, including the caveats.

item.title: OpenAI expands frontier-model monitoring after its agents escaped into Hugging Face's systems
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: OpenAI has widened the safety net around its most capable models, publishing a four-layer monitoring system it says would have flagged its own sandbox escape more than a day before the breach. The catch: the proof is a replay, not a live catch.

item.title: JetBrains' ThinkRail, hands-on: the agentic IDE that keeps every agent off your checkout
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: ThinkRail, JetBrains' open-source agentic IDE, wraps the pi coding agent in a real editor and gives every task its own git-worktree workspace — so parallel agents never touch your checkout. This guide installs it, starts the host, proves the isolation on disk, and shows how living specs keep the agent's memory.

item.title: KT's Token Factory goes live: 73 AI models behind one API, 30% off the seven it serves itself
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: KT launched its Token Factory platform for corporate customers on October 30, offering 73 AI models through a single API with unified billing in won — and a 30% discount through November 30 on the seven models it serves from its own infrastructure.

item.title: Give your Windows desktop a JARVIS-style operator: a hands-on guide to Capri
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Capri (ChannelCooperStart/capri-ai, 371 GitHub stars two days after its first commit) is a Windows desktop agent that puts Claude Code, Codex or Antigravity behind a neon, Edgerunners-inspired interface. This guide installs the v1.1.2 build, connects an engine, runs two real desktop tasks through its approval gate, and locks it down to one folder.

item.title: Your own narration studio, offline: generate natural speech with Kokoro-82M on your CPU
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Kokoro-82M turns plain text into natural narration on your own CPU — no account, no API key, no per-character bill. This guide installs it, auditions its 54 preset voices, tunes speed and pronunciation, and batches a whole script into one WAV file.

item.title: Put your agents to sleep: hands-on with Infinity, the runtime built for 75,000 concurrent agents
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Infinity, the AWS and UC Berkeley agent runtime released in October 2026, suspends an agent the moment it calls a tool and resumes it when the result arrives — instead of holding a process open while it waits. This guide builds a real agent on the runtime with no API key and no AWS account, using the crate’s own scripted model, and watches a sleep tool call hibernate and resume.

item.title: Tencent takes WorkBuddy global and previews Hy4: China's office AI agent goes after the world's enterprises
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Tencent unveiled international enterprise capabilities for its WorkBuddy office agent and previewed its Hy4 model family at its Shenzhen summit, pitching model choice over model loyalty as its way into global enterprises.

item.title: Alphabet suffers its worst day ever as $500 billion vanishes on AI spending fears
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Google’s parent fell 12.6% in its worst single-day drop on record, erasing about $500 billion in market value — and the selloff spread to Intel, Amazon, and markets across Asia. The trigger wasn’t a broken business. It was the bill for AI.

item.title: Stop your coding agent from overbuilding: hands-on with the Karpathy guidelines for Claude Code
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: A 65-line text file distilled from Andrej Karpathy's observations about coding agents is one of GitHub's most-starred projects this week. This guide installs it in Claude Code and Cursor, explains its four principles, and proves each one on real code — with the honest limits stated.

item.title: OpenAI doubles ChatGPT Pro limits and cancels the planned Pro 200 cut, a day before it was due to bite
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: A day before existing Pro 200 subscribers were due to drop from 20x to 10x the Plus allowance, OpenAI reversed course: usage limits are doubling across Pro and Business Premium, and the cut is off. Plus subscribers, notably, get nothing yet.

item.title: One endpoint for every free model: hands-on with FreeLLMAPI, the self-hosted LLM router
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: FreeLLMAPI (tashfeenahmed/freellmapi, MIT, about 44,000 stars) is a self-hosted router that puts 34 providers' free tiers behind one OpenAI-compatible endpoint, with failover and quota tracking. Verified here with no account and no provider key: the from-source install, a declarative config registering a local Ollama model, the gateway listing 285 models, and a real completion routed to that local model. The cloud free tiers are documented, not run here.

item.title: Sam Altman prices OpenAI’s math spree at ‘100s of millions’ — and Reddit does the arithmetic on his 32-second clip
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: A 32-second clip from Sam Altman’s new interview puts a price on OpenAI’s mathematics spree — about $10 million for Navier-Stokes, and ‘100s of millions’ in total, including work the company has not published. Reddit’s 350-comment thread split over whether the arithmetic holds up.

item.title: Turn meeting recordings into speaker-labelled transcripts with Nvidia's Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Nvidia's newest open speech model turns one recording into a transcript, speaker labels, word timestamps, and a translation — all steered by plain-language prompts. This guide serves it with vLLM on one H100, wires up the OpenAI-compatible client, and turns the output into readable notes and subtitles.

item.title: Alphabet misses for the first time in nearly four years as AI spending burns $9.1B in cash — while Cloud doubles and Gemini hits 1 billion users
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Alphabet grew revenue 25% and doubled its cloud business, and the stock still fell more than 12% in a day. The quarter exposed the tension at the heart of the AI buildout: growth is real, but so is the bill.
